relevance_note: Case series of HA20 patients with per-patient supplementary tables: "17 patients from 6 families with heterozygous likely loss-of-function variants in TNFAIP3 (ACMG class 4–5) were finally included."
method_note: Built with a short Python script from my own reading; every value was typed by me, no table was auto-transcribed. Labels: the text names pt1-pt4, p7, p10, p14, pt13, pt15, Pt16 and pt17 (each in the only or most frequent form the text uses for that person); patients 5, 6, 8, 9, 11 and 12 are named only by the bare 'Pt' number column of Supplementary File 1, so they are labelled 'Supplementary File 1 #<n>'. Family membership, the family's variant and ACMG class come from Supplementary File 1, where Family, Variant and ACMG class are printed once per family row and apply to every patient listed in that row's Pt cell. Stacked cells (v6, D-31): in Supplementary File 1 (Age at analysis, Age at onset, Recurrent fever, Oral aphthosis, Genital ulcers, Gastrointestinal disease, Arthritis/tenosynovitis, Skin disease, NPI, Autoimmunity, IS, CXCL9, CXCL10, PGA, CRP) and Supplementary File 3 (ANA, Other autoimmune laboratory findings, Treatments), every multi-patient family row (families 1, 2, 3, 5, 6) holds ' / '-separated stacked values (often fewer values than patients) with no per-patient labels, so none of them was assigned to a person; this includes cells whose stacked values are all identical (e.g. ANA 'Negative / Negative / Negative / Negative' in family 1, NPI '+ / + / + / + / +' in family 6). Single '+' cells in multi-patient rows were also not assigned. Only family 4 (patient 9, one patient) was read from these tables. '+' read as present; empty cells and NA as not reported; '-' in Supplementary File 3 is not defined in the legend, so not used. Ages in Supplementary File 1 have no printed unit; ISO durations for patient 9 assume years (cohort ages up to 71; Figure 2 gives onset ages in years). The asterisks in the Pt column mark parents (*) and grandparents (**) per the table footnote: patients 4, 6, 8, 11 and 16 are parents, 12 and 17 grandparents; whose parent is not stated (pedigrees only in a figure), so no inheritance was recorded. 'All but one variants were inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern' is a general statement and not used for inheritance. The exon 7-9 deletion (patient 9) is called 'de novo' but parental testing is not described, so inheritance is not reported (rule 8). Zygosity heterozygous for all 17 from the statement naming the 17 included patients; ethnicity 'European' from 'All 17 patients were European'. 'truncating variants resulting in stop codon' is a group statement listing no enum class, so variant type is not reported except the exon 7-9 deletion, which the text calls a copy number variation. SLE excluded for all 17 from 'none of the patients in our cohort fulfilled the classification criteria for SLE' (named group). Neuropsychiatric diagnoses (ADHD, anxiety, mood dysregulation, ODD, pica, depression) were recorded as features but not mapped to the checklist item 'central nervous system involvement'. Sex: only a group count (12 female of 17), so not reported per person. One suicide attempt is attributed to 'one case' of Pt16/pt17 without saying which, so not recorded. Patient 9: 'Gastrointestinal disease +' mapped to the checklist item gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation; ANA negative recorded as positive ANA excluded, but 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' left not reported because other antibodies are marked '-' (undefined); CRP 0.54 mg/dl not interpreted as elevated. Three previously published people from the Discussion are included: Duan et al^31 patient (de novo frameshift, NPSLE; no variant printed; 'de novo' without described parental testing, so inheritance not reported), the ^32 patient (T674P, progressive neuroinflammation, baricitinib) and the proband of the ^36 family (cutaneous disease; 'the same TNFAIP3 variant' is not printed, so variant_original_string not reported). Other cited cohorts (Yu, Aeschlimann, Karri, Elhani, Kadowaki, ref 9) give only group-level data and get no rows. No internal contradictions found; Table 1 group counts were not used for individuals.
